gloss: to spout; to burst out laughing

definitions.gloss: to spout; to gush out; to spray
definitions.explanation: For liquids or gases to suddenly emerge forcefully from an opening.

definitions.gloss: to burst out laughing; to crack up
definitions.explanation: To suddenly and involuntarily start laughing, often when trying to hold it in.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}が{管|かん}から{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Water gushed out from the pipe.

examples.japanese: {間欠泉|かんけつせん}が{熱湯|ねっとう}を{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}す。
{傷口|きずぐち}から{血|ち}が{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}している。
examples.english: Blood is gushing from the wound.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}て{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I burst out laughing when I saw his face.

examples.japanese: {真面目|まじめ}な{場面|ばめん}で{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しそうになった。
examples.english: I almost burst out laughing during a serious moment.

examples.japanese: おかしくて{飲|の}んでいたお{茶|ちゃ}を{思|おも}わず{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}してしまった。
examples.english: It was so funny I involuntarily spit out the tea I was drinking.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Compound verb: {吹|ふ}く + {出|だ}す.

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action for sense 1 ({水|みず}が{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}している = water is gushing).

NUANCE: The {出|だ}す component emphasizes the sudden start of the action. In sense 2, it suggests an involuntary outburst.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{思|おも}わず{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}す: to burst out laughing unintentionally
・{噴水|ふんすい}が{水|みず}を{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}す: a fountain spouts water
